source_caption:
Shooter — The Wrong Man to Frame

Shooter (2007) follows Bob Lee Swagger, a highly skilled former Marine sniper who retreats into isolation after a mission ends in tragedy. Haunted by his past, Swagger wants nothing more than to live peacefully, far away from the military world he once knew.

His life changes when government officials approach him for help preventing an assassination. Using his extensive knowledge of weapons, tactics, and long-range shooting, Swagger agrees to assist. However, the mission turns into a setup when he is framed for the very assassination he was recruited to stop.

Now hunted by law enforcement and betrayed by people he once trusted, Swagger must escape capture and uncover the truth behind the conspiracy. With enemies closing in, he relies on his precision, intelligence, and survival instincts to expose the powerful individuals responsible.

The film explores themes of betrayal, corruption, justice, loyalty, and revenge. It shows how a trained soldier can become a target when he discovers secrets that powerful people are desperate to protect.

What makes Shooter compelling is watching Swagger use his military expertise to outsmart his pursuers and turn the hunt against those who framed him.

💬 They thought they could silence him—but they chose the wrong man to hunt.

source_details.synopsis: Shooter is a 2007 American action thriller film directed by Antoine Fuqua and written by Jonathan Lemkin, based on the 1993 novel Point of Impact by Stephen Hunter. The film follows Force Recon Marine Scout Sniper veteran Bob Lee Swagger (Mark Wahlberg), who is framed for murder by a mercenary unit operating for a private military firm. The film also stars Michael Peña, Danny Glover, Kate Mara, Levon Helm, and Ned Beatty. Shooter was produced by Lorenzo di Bonaventura through di Bonaventura Pictures, and released by Paramount Pictures in the United States on March 23, 2007. The film received mixed reviews and grossed $95.7 million on a $61 million budget.
